problem: LLM-based visual navigation relies on heavy text prompt engineering, converting observations and history into long text for frozen text-only LLMs, which are poorly suited to non-text modalities such as images, GPS and compass.
motivation: Multimodal LLMs are fine-tuned on image-text pairs for VQA, so fine-tuning on observation-action pairs could yield a navigation policy without complex prompt systems. Navigation is a long-horizon, partially observed task, so the LLM needs a compact memory of the past and dense supervision.
key_idea: Fine-tune a frozen-LLaMA-13B multimodal LLM (only projection layers trained) with a simple prompt, current image tokens, and GRU history tokens, outputting a text action probability distribution built from a BC teacher, human labels and collision masking.
insight: Outputting a probability distribution rather than a single action is crucial: Success 0.6790 vs 0.4610 for direct action output. A GRU history collector far outperforms feeding 15 consecutive observations (0.4610 vs 0.0910). Zeroing colliding actions in the target improves Success (0.6510 to 0.6790) and lowers collisions (39.78 to 27.76). Zero-shot MiniGPT4 gets 0% success, so fine-tuning is needed.
method: History collector: ResNet-50 for visual features plus linear layers for GPS, compass, previous action and goal, fed to a GRU; pretrained with PIRLNav behavior cloning and kept frozen; it also yields an action probability vector.
Observation encoder: frozen BLIP-2 ViT plus Q-former encodes the current RGB image only; GPS and compass gave no benefit here.
Projection layers (only trained part): Q-former plus linear layer maps history features to 32 history tokens; a linear layer maps observation features to 32 observation tokens.
Text prompt: ChatGPT-paraphrased template containing goal category, image tokens, history tokens and the history collector's action probabilities written as text.
LLM: frozen LLaMA-13B takes text, history and observation tokens and outputs actions as text probabilities.
Target construction: P = CollisionCheck&Renorm(0.8*P_SOTA(IL) + 0.2*P_gt one-hot); colliding actions are zeroed and the vector renormalized.
Training: 80k iterations, batch size 6, on the 77k-demonstration HM3D human dataset from PIRLNav.

setting.backbone: LLaMA-13B (frozen) + BLIP-2 ViT/Q-former (frozen) + ResNet-50/GRU history collector (frozen after BC pretraining) + trained projection layers
setting.training_data: 77k human object-goal demonstrations from 80 HM3D training scenes (PIRLNav dataset); about 80k iterations x batch 6 (roughly 4.8k-9.6k episodes seen)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + GPS + compass (plus previous action and goal category in the history model)
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: stop, forward 0.25 m, turn left/right 30°, look up/down 30°
setting.privileged: none at test time (collision signals used only in training targets)

numbers.eval_set_note: 2k episodes on the 20 HM3D-Semantics validation scenes, following PIRLNav's evaluation; 500-action limit, 1 m success radius
numbers.extra: trained on human demonstrations; history collector distilled from PIRLNav IL; 6 object categories
outputs a single action instead of probabilities

numbers_note: Success and SoftSPL are printed as fractions in [0,1] in the paper and kept as printed. HM3D validation split is labeled 'val'.
results: The method reaches 0.6790 Success / 0.3723 SoftSPL on HM3D ObjectNav, beating the strongest baseline RL_Ft (0.6615 / 0.3604) and IL (0.5980 / 0.3051). Collision count drops from 39.78 to 27.76 with the collision check.
limitations: Gain over the RL-finetuned BC baseline is small (0.6790 vs 0.6615) and the method depends on a pretrained IL teacher and history collector.
Only six object categories, HM3D only, no real-robot experiments; evaluated on a 2k-episode subset.
LLM is frozen and only projections are trained; collision handling is a simple target mask; RL fine-tuning of LLMs is left unsolved.
